quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If a tire blows out, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brake hard and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and brake gently.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out while driving, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car going straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and braking gently. Do not stop on the road. Pull off the road to a safe place.

questions.question: You cannot see other vehicles because of dust or smoke on the road. What should you turn on?

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights any time you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: You are traveling in the wrong direction.
Treat it like a stop sign.
Wait until it turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light ahead and have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the light turns red.
Slow down and go through carefully.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: At a steady yellow light, stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: Which statement is false?

options.text: Heavier people need more alcohol to raise their blood alcohol content (BAC).
Between two people of the same weight, the one with more body fat will show intoxication signs first.
Drinking three drinks in one hour affects you the same as drinking three drinks in three hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking three drinks in one hour affects you the same as drinking three drinks in three hours.
questions.explanation: Drinking faster causes stronger intoxication. Drinking three drinks in one hour affects you more than drinking three drinks over three hours. Heavier people need more alcohol to raise their BAC. People with more body fat get intoxicated faster than people with less body fat, when they weigh the same.

questions.question: You are entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane. What should you do?

options.text: Enter the right lane and speed up to match traffic immediately.
Use the shoulder to speed up to match traffic.
Speed up and enter only when you see a gap in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up and enter only when you see a gap in traffic.
questions.explanation: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, wait for a gap in traffic. Speed up only after you have identified a clear gap.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the way is clear.
You can pass on the left when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the way is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross it to pass on the left when it is safe.

questions.question: A car cuts in front of you suddenly. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk your horn and brake hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car merges too close in front of you, release the gas pedal. This creates space between you and the other car without slamming on the brakes or swerving.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels run off the pavement edge. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to edge back onto the pavement.
Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently.
Brake hard and turn the wheel sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and brake gently. Slow down, check traffic, and look for a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: If a tire blows out suddenly, how should you use the brakes?

options.text: Use them lightly.
Pump them.
Apply them firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use them lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out while driving, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car going straight. Slow down by releasing the gas pedal and braking lightly.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Directions for children
School zone ahead
Playground area ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone ahead
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that you are in or near a school zone. Watch for children and obey the speed limit.

questions.question: Someone is tailgating you on a two-lane road. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down gradually so they pass you.
Speed up to increase distance between cars.
Tap your brakes to slow down, then resume speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually so they pass you.
questions.explanation: If someone is following too closely, slow down gradually. This encourages them to pass you. If you can, change lanes first.

questions.question: When you change your address, how long do you have to notify the Department of Safety?

options.text: Within 6 months
Within 10 days
Within 45 days

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 10 days
questions.explanation: You must notify the Department of Safety within 10 days if your address changes.

questions.question: You see heavy smoke ahead on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
Turn on high beam headlights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: Reduce speed immediately. Move to the right and stop off the road. Check if it is safe before continuing. Smoke can hurt your eyes and lungs.

questions.question: You park uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the edge of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the edge of the road
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the road edge. If your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic, not into it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to watch for bicycles, pedestrians, and other hazards.

questions.question: Your car starts to skid. What should you do?

options.text: Brake lightly.
Do not use the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not brake during a skid. Braking makes the skid worse.

questions.question: You parallel park facing downhill. How should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the road edge.
Turn them away from the road edge.
Keep them straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply toward the road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or road edge. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with siren and lights is approaching while you are in an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection.
Pull right and stop before finishing the intersection.
Finish crossing, then pull right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing, then pull right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection, finish crossing it. Then pull to the right and stop. Always yield to emergency vehicles with sirens and flashing lights.

questions.question: What does a stop sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if other cars are near.
Come to a full stop, then go when safe.
Proceed carefully without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: Always come to a complete stop at a stop sign. Stop at the marked line, crosswalk, or before the intersection. Only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain just starts.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain just starts.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with rainwater and create a slick film.

questions.question: When should you be most careful while turning or stopping in rain?

options.text: After it has rained all day.
Half an hour after rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Car oil has not yet washed off the pavement and mixes with rain to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: You are not in the proper lane to turn at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and wait for a gap to turn.
Stop and wait until the way is clear before turning.
Go to the next intersection to make the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection to make the turn.
questions.explanation: Never turn from the wrong lane. Drive to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane there. Circle back if needed.

questions.question: After a reportable accident, how long do you have to file a report with the Department of Safety and Homeland Security?

options.text: 10 days.
20 days.
48 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: 20 days.
questions.explanation: The driver and/or owner of any vehicle in a reportable crash in Tennessee must file a report within 20 days, no matter who is at fault.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left and parked vehicles are to your right. Which way should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
Between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: Steer in the middle between the oncoming cars and the parked cars.

questions.question: What should you do when driving at night?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because visibility is lower. It is harder to judge speed and distance. Increase your following distance to stop safely if the car ahead stops suddenly.

questions.question: Your view at an intersection is blocked. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see clearly.
questions.explanation: Slow down at intersections. If you cannot see clearly, stop and inch forward until you can see traffic in both directions.

questions.question: You are turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. Which lane should you enter?

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the first available legal lane. When turning onto a one-way street, enter the first lane.

questions.question: You are entering the interstate. You found a gap and matched your speed. What is your next step?

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to clear completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: After finding a gap and matching traffic speed, signal and merge carefully. Watch other traffic and do not assume other drivers will make room for you.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a small car.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or move to another lane. Do not brake suddenly.
